A soaring barrel-vaulted palm nave, its riveted iron ribs arcing up and off both top corners of the frame, slim white-painted glazing ribs fanning between the panes overhead and the wet glazed flank running out past the left edge; a brass spiral stair climbs the near pier to a slatted catwalk that runs the whole length at canopy height, seen obliquely from the edge of the sunken bed, looking up along the ribs.

A tiered glasshouse built like a wedding cake, three round glazed storeys stepping inward, each ring smaller than the one below; the nearest ring of curved panes fills the right third of the frame and its iron ring-beam crosses the top, a bronze stair spiralling up through a hole in each tier, seen from the second tier's walkway looking across and down through the open middle.

A great dome raised over an oak that stood here first, the trunk breaking straight up through the brick floor and the ironwork shaped around it in a ring of shorter ribs; the dome's wet panes fill the upper frame and run off the top-left corner, a plank catwalk circling the trunk at branch height on brass brackets, seen from the floor beside the trunk looking up and along the ring.

A long glasshouse standing out from a cliff on iron stilts, its floor a grating you can see daylight through, the curved glazed roof arcing off the top of the frame and the outer glass wall filling the whole right edge, a short ladder-stair up to a narrow inspection walk under the ridge, seen from the inner end looking along the house with the beds falling away.

A small ornate glasshouse standing complete INSIDE a far larger one, its own little glazed pitched roof and brass finial rising in the middle distance while the great house's ribs and panes arch high above and off both top corners; a stair goes up the big house's flank to a gallery, seen from that gallery half-height, looking down onto the little roof among the palms.

Two houses through one inner glass wall: a hot jungle nave in front, its wet panes filling the upper frame and running off the left edge, and beyond the misted inner glass a cold frost-fern house going pale and blue; an iron stair in the near corner rises to a catwalk that crosses above the dividing wall, seen from beside the connecting door, obliquely.

A long curving lean-to glasshouse laid against an old brick garden wall, the brick warm and trained with fruit down the whole left side, the single-slope glazed roof running up out of the top-right corner with its slim ribs in a shallow fan; a plank step-up and a running board along the wall at waist height, seen from the low end three-quarters along, looking up the curve.

An octagonal glazed pavilion crowned with a brass lantern top, its eight iron corner-posts standing in the beds and the curved panes of two faces filling the left and upper frame, a tight cast-iron stair winding up to a railed ring under the lantern, seen from one corner of the floor looking diagonally across to the far post.

The fan-shaped apse end of a great nave, the ribs radiating from a single high boss like the spokes of an umbrella and running off the top and right of the frame, every pane above beaded with water; an iron gallery crosses the mouth of the apse on slim columns, seen from the side aisle below, oblique, looking up into the fan.

A sunken pit-house whose floor lies a full storey below the garden, so the glazed sides start at knee height and the glass roof sits low and close overhead, crossing the whole top of the frame; brick steps with a brass handrail climb out at the far end, seen from the bottom of the steps looking along the low warm tunnel of beds.

A three-storey glass tower with an open well down the middle, iron galleries ringing the well at each floor and the tall glazed flank filling the right of the frame from floor to ceiling with its ribs cropped by the top edge; a bolted iron stair zigzags up one side, seen from the first gallery looking obliquely across the well and up.

A glasshouse bridging a canal, its arched glazed roof springing from parapet to parapet and arcing off both top corners, a strip of thick glass set into the floor so green water-light comes up through it onto the leaves; a few steps and a landing at one end, seen from the middle of the span looking along it at an angle.

A long low vinery under a ridge-and-furrow roof, the glazed folds running away in a zigzag across the top of the frame and the near fold cropped by the upper-left corner, vine rods trained along wires just under the glass; a rolling plank platform on cast wheels to reach the ridge, seen from beside it, looking down the furrows.

A glasshouse roofed over an abandoned stone quarry, the raw cut rock face making the whole back wall and the iron-and-glass roof spanning the pit from rim to rim, its ribs crossing the upper frame and running off to the right; stone-cut steps and an iron handrail climb the rock to a bolted walkway, seen from the quarry floor looking up the face.

A glasshouse raised over a steaming hot spring, the rock pools breathing white vapour into the roof space, the glazed ribs arcing overhead into haze and running off the top-left corner while the wet glass flank fills the right edge; duckboards and a short brass-railed stair to a viewing deck, seen from the duckboards beside the nearest pool.

A vast single dome with a ring catwalk at half-height and a chain hoist hanging from the central boss, the riveted ribs converging high above and cropped by the top of the frame, condensation running down the curved panes that fill the left edge; the catwalk reached by a spiral stair in the near pier, seen from the floor looking up past the hoist chain.

A conservatory the size of a railway shed, one enormous iron arch after another marching away down the house, the nearest arch cropped at both top corners and the glazed end wall a soft bright haze far off; an iron gantry walk runs along the springing line of the arches, seen from under the second arch, obliquely across the beds.

A glasshouse framed like an upturned boat, its curved iron ribs closing overhead exactly as a hull's would, the ribs running off the top of the frame and the glazed flank off the left; a narrow keel-walk of planks down the centre and a short stair to a stern platform, seen from beside the walk looking up into the ribs.

A glazed crossing where two great naves meet at right angles, four iron piers carrying a raised octagon of glass above, ribs radiating from it across the whole top of the frame and one nave's flank glass filling the right edge; stairs climb two of the piers to a balcony ring, seen from under the crossing looking diagonally down one nave.

A conservatory grafted straight onto the side of a stone house, so its inner wall is the house's own dressed masonry with two lit windows in it, the glazed roof sweeping up from that wall and off the top-right corner, the outer panes filling the lower right; a few stone steps and a landing to the house door, seen from the far corner of the beds, oblique.

A low propagating house, roof close enough overhead to touch, its glazed slope crossing the top of the frame and the near glass wall cropped down the left edge, benches running the length at hip height on iron legs; a single step up to a raised end bench, seen from the aisle between the benches, looking along it at an angle.

A tall glasshouse with a working brass lift in an open iron cage standing right in the middle of the floor, its guide rails going straight up through the roof space to a gallery, the dome's ribs and panes arcing off both top corners behind it; the gallery also reached by a stair, seen from beside the cage looking up and past it.

An amphitheatre glasshouse, the beds stepping down in curved terraces to a pool at the bottom, the glazed roof arching over the whole bowl and cropped at the top of the frame, the flank panes running off the right edge; a curved stair follows the terraces down, seen from three steps up, looking obliquely across the bowl.

A lily house, a shallow warm pool taking nearly the whole floor with only a narrow brick margin round it, the low glazed roof close above the water and crossing the entire top of the frame, its ribs doubled in the reflection; a short stair to a corner platform over the water, seen from the brick margin at the pool's shoulder.

A glasshouse whose end wall is one great curved bay of hundreds of small panes bowing outward, the bay filling the right half of the frame from floor to ribs and the roof's ironwork running off the top-left; a plank gallery crosses the bay at half height on brass brackets, seen from the floor to one side, looking up into the curve.

A glasshouse built on the flat roof of a brick mill, its glazed walls rising from the parapet on all sides, the nearest riveted iron arch crossing the top of the frame and a beaded wet glazed flank filling the right edge while the mill's coping stone runs below; a ladder-stair climbs the near parapet corner to the duckboard floor inside, seen from under the nearest arch, obliquely.

A round house whose whole floor is a turntable slowly rotating the beds, its ring of curved panes rising to a central lantern whose riveted ribs fan out and off both top corners of the frame, slim glazing ribs crossing the wet overhead panes in radiating lines and the nearest iron pier standing broad in the foreground; a slatted catwalk circles at canopy height on brass brackets, seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs.

A glazed cloister running around all four sides of an open stone court, its lean-to glazed roof filling the upper frame and running off the top-right corner, riveted iron wall-posts carrying slim glazing ribs down to the brick sill while the stone court drops away below the inner rail; a plank gallery on brass brackets steps back along the inner face, seen from a gallery at half height, looking down across the beds.

A north-light house under a saw-tooth roof, the glazed slopes all facing one way, their riveted iron frames crossing the top of the frame in repeating triangles and the beaded wet panes filling the upper half while opaque back-slopes alternate in shadow below; a chain-hoist hangs from the ridge and a ring catwalk circles the nearest valley post on brass collars, seen from the sunken bed, looking up and along.

A glasshouse on an island in a lake, water on every side of the glass, the curved glazed roof arcing off the top of the frame and a beaded wet glazed wall filling the right edge while the lake surface catches the ironwork in a silver band below the sill; a running board at waist height runs the inner perimeter on iron brackets, seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across.

A dome with a ring bridge suspended inside on chains from the boss, the chains rising in four taut curves to the iron crown-ring while the dome's beaded wet panes fill the upper frame and arc off both top corners, slim white glazing ribs fanning between each riveted rib overhead; a cast-iron stair winds up the near pier to the suspended walkway, seen from the catwalk, looking down through the leaves.

A glasshouse in an old railway roundhouse, the turntable pit at its centre holding the iron pivot ring flush with the brick floor, the curved glazed roof running off the top of the frame and the nearest glazed bay filling the right edge, riveted ring-beams crossing overhead at each radial pier; a bolted iron stair climbs the far pier to a slatted upper gallery, seen from the far end, looking along the house obliquely.

A glass tunnel driven straight through a hillside, its curved barrel vault of riveted iron hoops and slim glazing ribs running from the near end off into the far circle of daylight, beaded wet panes filling the overhead frame and cropping off both top corners, the brick floor damp between the beds; a brass spiral stair climbs the near pier to a ridge catwalk threading the whole length, seen from the foot of the stair, looking up into the roof.

A corridor of glass arches along a canal towpath, each riveted iron arch stepping away in diminishing rings down the frame, beaded wet panes filling the curved flanks and the nearest arch-ring crossing the top edge, brick piers anchoring every springing point; stone steps with a brass handrail rise at the near corner to a flagged upper walkway above the barge-side glass, seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across.

A glass corridor slung between two brick towers, its floor a long iron bridge of open grating with the drop visible below, the glazed barrel roof arcing off both top corners and the riveted side-beams running the full length at mid-frame, slim glazing ribs fanning up from each flange; a railed inspection walk runs the outer edge above the beds, seen from a gallery at half height, looking down across the beds.

A house built as a glass staircase up a slope, each landing a glazed room stepping higher than the last, the riveted iron sills and slim glazing ribs crossing the upper frame and the wet panes of the topmost room running off the right edge into light; a running board at waist height follows every riser along the uphill wall, seen from the sunken bed at the foot, looking up and along the climbing landings.

A house on a spiral plan winding inward like a snail shell, the glass roof coiling with it in narrowing rings of riveted iron and beaded wet panes that arc up and off both top corners of the frame, each curved bay tighter than the last; a chain-hoist hangs from the central ring-beam and a ring catwalk circles the inner court on brass brackets, seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs.

A house whose glazed roof rolls back on rails, one half already open to the sky, the iron rail-beam crossing the full width of the upper frame and the remaining panes filling the left half while the right half shows open ironwork against pale air; a brass spiral stair climbs the closed gable to a small platform at rail height, seen from under the nearest arch, obliquely.

A glasshouse hung off a cliff face on iron brackets, empty air below the iron grating floor, the curved glazed roof arcing up and off the top of the frame and the outer glass wall filling the whole right edge in beaded wet panes; a slatted catwalk runs the outer flank on riveted bracket-arms above the grating, seen from the catwalk itself, looking down through the vine rods and the open grid into the air below.

A house whose iron ribs are cast as palm trunks, the fronds spreading at their crowns to form the roof brackets, each riveted frond-arm carrying slim glazing ribs that fan up and off the top corners of the frame, the beaded wet panes between them catching the light; a ladder-stair mounts the nearest trunk-pier to a slatted catwalk at frond height, seen from the far end, looking along the house obliquely.

A stone orangery with tall round-arched windows down the near flank, their keystoned reveals filling the right edge of the frame, a glazed roof added above on slim riveted iron rafters that cross the top and run off both upper corners, beaded panes catching the light between brass glazing bars; a plank gallery on brass brackets runs the full length of the stone wall above the arch crowns, seen from the foot of the stair, looking up into the roof.

A curvilinear house whose roofs rise and fall in glazed waves along its length, each crest a riveted iron ridge-ring and each valley a gutter on paired brackets, the undulating panes filling the upper frame and rolling off the right edge while the nearest wave-crest crosses the top left corner; stone steps with a brass handrail climb the near end pier to a half-height gallery, seen from that gallery, looking down across the beds.

A glasshouse wrapped around the base of a stone lighthouse tower, its curved iron ribs radiating outward from the tower's rough courses and the glazed roof arcing up to meet the dressed stone before running off the top of the frame, beaded wet panes filling the upper curve and the glazed drum wall closing the right edge; a railed inspection walk circles the tower at shoulder height on bolted iron brackets, seen from the sunken bed, looking up and along.

A corridor house a quarter of a mile long, its single glazed vault of riveted iron ribs and slim white glazing bars running to a bright vanishing point, the nearest rib crossing the top of the frame and the glazed flank filling the left edge, duckboards laid along the central path between the brick piers; a bolted iron stair in the near corner rises to a ridge walkway running the length, seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across.

A glasshouse in the bottom of a dry dock, its glass roof below the quay walls, the pitched glazed slope filling the upper frame entirely with beaded wet panes and slim glazing ribs while the riveted iron wall-plate beds into the dock's stone courses on both sides; a cast-iron stair winds up the near dock wall through a glazed sleeve to the catwalk at quay level, seen from the catwalk, looking down through the leaves.

A lean-to glasshouse pressed against a castle curtain wall, its pitched glazed roof rising to meet the dressed stone and the arrow slits showing dark in the ashlar behind the brick beds; slim white glazing ribs fan up from the front rail to the ridge iron, the wet panes running off the top-right corner and the long glazed flank filling the left edge entire; a brass spiral stair climbs the far pier, seen from the far end looking along the house obliquely.

A glass hangar with sliding end doors standing open, the house tall enough for a balloon, its soaring ridge iron crossing the upper frame and the riveted side columns running off both top corners; the glazed end wall fills the right third, its panes beaded and catching the light in horizontal bands, and the stone floor flags step up at the near edge with a brass handrail rising beside them; seen from the foot of the stair looking up into the roof.

A house roofed in overlapping fish-scale panes, the curved ribs bowing under them and the nearest pier rising from the brick floor to fill the left foreground; the scalloped glass crosses the top of the frame and runs off both upper corners, slim riveted ribs fanning between each scale and a cast-iron stair winding up the far pier into the canopy; seen from the floor beside the nearest pier looking up along the ribs.

A house half sunk into a lake, its lower panes looking out under green water and the iron arches rising from a submerged brick sill; the upper glazed wall fills the right edge and the wet panes of the roof arc off the top-left corner, a chain-hoist hanging from the ridge beam above a ring catwalk that circles the inner arch on brass brackets; seen from under the nearest arch obliquely, looking up and across.

A glasshouse a stream runs straight through, its brick channel entering under the near glass wall and leaving under the far one, the water carrying light up into the beaded panes; riveted ribs arc up and off both top corners and the glazed flank fills the right edge, a slatted catwalk spanning the channel on iron brackets and running the whole length at mid-height; seen from the far end looking along the house obliquely.

A double-height house with a full iron mezzanine floor slung across its middle, its riveted ribs climbing past the mezzanine and arcing off both top corners of the frame, slim glazing ribs fanning between beaded wet panes overhead while the plank gallery on brass brackets crosses the full width at mid-height, its duckboards level with the eye; seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across the iron grid of the floor below and up into the vaulted panes.

A glass barrel vault flung across a ravine, rock faces filling both side edges of the frame and the iron grating of the floor showing the drop beneath, riveted arch-ribs sweeping up and off the top corners while slim glazing ribs carry the wet panes across the crown; a bolted iron stair rises from a rock ledge on the near side to the catwalk running the barrel's length; seen from the catwalk, looking down through the leaves into the ravine below.

The inner courtyard of a mansion roofed over in glass, stone-mullioned windows rising on every side and the nearest pier filling the left foreground, riveted iron ribs springing from stone corbels and crossing the top of the frame in a fan of slim glazing bars over beaded wet panes; a railed inspection walk girdles the courtyard at first-floor height on bracketed iron arms; seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs into the glazed vault.

A glasshouse roofed inside the roofless nave of a ruined abbey, old stone arches standing on both sides and the new iron-and-glass barrel spanning between them, riveted ribs seated on the carved string-course and slim glazing ribs carrying beaded wet panes up and off the top of the frame; a ladder-stair of bolted flat iron rises against the nearest pier to a catwalk level with the springing line; seen from the foot of the stair, looking up into the roof.

A cruciform house with a glass lantern tower rising over the crossing, its square riveted collar climbing straight up through the centre of the frame and the four barrel arms running off all edges, slim glazing ribs fanning from the collar into beaded wet panes that fill the upper corners; a running board on brass clips skirts the crossing at waist height and continues into each arm; seen from under the nearest arch, obliquely, the lantern tower receding above.

A house whose glazed end gable carries a great clock face, its hands seen from inside, the brass numerals glinting through beaded wet panes that fill the far end of the frame and run off both top corners, slim glazing ribs fanning up from the clock ring to the barrel vault overhead; a bolted iron stair climbs the near wall to a slatted catwalk crossing the width at mid-height, seen from the sunken bed, looking up and along the riveted nave.

A glasshouse built around a waterfall that drops from a rock shelf inside it, the rushing column centred in the frame while riveted iron ribs arc up and off both top corners and beaded wet panes sheet the curved flanks; a cast-iron stair winds up the near pier past the rock shelf, its treads bright with mist, seen from a gallery at half height, looking down across the beds and the white plunge below.

A glasshouse that is a bridge across a river gorge, its floor the iron-grating span itself, the glazed barrel roof arcing off the top of the frame and both glazed flanks running out past the left and right edges, slim riveted ribs crossing the curved panes overhead; a slatted catwalk runs the ridge above, reached by a short ladder at the near pier, seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across the gorge below.

A glasshouse braced with old ship masts and rigging inside, the glass hung from them, the tallest mast rising through the ridge and its stays fanning out to the riveted iron ring-beams, beaded wet panes filling the curved roof and running off both top corners; a brass spiral stair winds up the nearest mast past belayed rope and brass cleats to a slatted platform under the ridge, seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs.

A glasshouse built on the deck of a canal barge, its glazed roof low over the hold, the curved panes crossing the top of the frame and the riveted iron gunwale-beams locking the glazed flanks to the teak deck, slim glazing ribs fanning between the side lights; a chain-hoist hangs from the ridge beam and a ring catwalk circles the hold on brass brackets just below the eaves, seen from the far end, looking along the house obliquely.

A cathedral-height palm house with two tiers of iron galleries ringing the walls, its riveted ribs climbing and arcing off both top corners of the frame while slim glazing ribs fan between the panes overhead and the wet beaded glass runs down the full right flank; a railed inspection walk cantilevered on brass brackets circles the upper tier, seen from the catwalk looking down through the palm canopy to the brick floor far below.

A glasshouse on the roof of a railway station, the train shed vaults visible below through its floor glass, the near riveted rib crossing the top of the frame and curved panes filling the left third while the iron floor grating lets the vaulted arches drop away in perspective beneath your feet; a plank gallery on brass brackets runs the long flank at half height, seen from under the nearest arch obliquely, looking along the glazed hull.

A glasshouse built on a railway carriage standing on a siding, glazed from floor to roof, its riveted corner posts rising to a ridge beam that crosses the top of the frame and the full curved glass wall filling the right edge, beaded panes running to the far end while vine rods climb the inner ironwork; stone steps with a brass handrail rise from the trackside ballast to the carriage door, seen from the sunken bed looking up and along the ridge.

A folly glasshouse shaped like a Gothic chapel, pointed glazed arches rising and running off both top corners of the frame while the glass steeple climbs the centre and its slim iron tracery fans into the apex above, beaded panes filling every lancet from sill to crown; a running board at waist height brackets along the nave flank on iron knees, seen from the foot of the stair looking up into the vaulted glass roof.

A hexagonal glasshouse with a raised clerestory of small panes around its crown, the clerestory ring crossing the upper frame and its iron mullions dividing the light while the six curved lower bays fill downward and the nearest riveted hip rib runs off the top-right corner; a ladder-stair climbs the inner face of the nearest pier to the gallery rail, seen from a gallery at half height looking down across the duckboard beds to the brick floor below.

Three parallel span-roof houses joined at their ends by one long glazed corridor, the nearest span's riveted iron ribs arcing up and off both top corners of the frame while the corridor's ridge-bar crosses the right edge and its beaded panes fill that flank; a slatted catwalk runs the full width where all three spans meet the corridor wall, its brass brackets catching the light from the clerestory above; seen from a gallery at half height, looking down across the beds.

A run of narrow peach cases along a brick wall, each a shallow glass box of its own, the sloping glazed lids stepping along the wall and their slim white-painted ribs fanning up to the brick coping, the nearest lid's beaded panes filling the whole upper frame and running off the right edge, the wall's iron tie-rods anchoring each case in turn; stone steps with a brass handrail rise at the near end; seen from the catwalk, looking down through the leaves.

A fernery grotto of tufa rock walls under a glass roof, the rough stone piers rising on both sides and the slim glazing ribs arcing between them overhead, beaded wet panes filling the upper frame and running off the top-left corner, dripping stone ledges stepping down both flanks, a plank gallery on brass brackets spanning the grotto at mid-height and its duckboard decking catching the green filtered light; seen from the far end, looking along the house obliquely.

A low pineapple stove house with brick tan-bark pits under a close glazed slope, the lean-to glass running from the low front wall up and off the top of the frame in slim riveted glazing ribs, the brick pit-walls stepping down the floor in a row and a squat iron flue pier rising at the far end; a cast-iron stair winds up the rear wall to the ridge vent, seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs.

A glasshouse on stilts over a marsh, reeds showing through the iron grating of the floor, the curved glazed roof arcing up and off both top corners of the frame and its riveted ring-beam crossing the upper third, the stilts' brass collar-rings descending into the dim space below the grating; a chain-hoist hangs from the central crown-iron and a ring catwalk on brass brackets circles the house at eave height; seen from the foot of the stair, looking up into the roof.

A glasshouse built round an old stone well head with its winding gear, the iron drum and chain rising at centre while riveted ribs arc up and off both top corners and slim glazing ribs fan between the wet panes overhead; a ladder-stair climbs the nearest pier to a slatted catwalk circling the well at canopy height, seen from under the nearest arch, obliquely.

A glass lantern tower with staircases in two flanking brick turrets, its tall glazed drum filling the upper frame and the riveted ring-beam crossing just below the crown, slim white glazing ribs fanning up to the apex while the near turret's brick pier fills the left edge; a railed inspection walk rings the drum at mid-height, seen from the sunken bed, looking up and along.

A glasshouse standing out over a lake on an iron pier, water showing under the grating in broken silver panels, the curved glazed roof arcing off the top of the frame and the outer glass wall filling the right edge, riveted ribs running from pier to ridge; a running board at waist height carries along the iron flank, seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across.

A square glass atrium with three tiers of iron balconies ringing it, each tier's bolted rail and duckboard walk stepping inward above the one below, the glazed roof crossing the top of the frame and the nearest balcony face filling the left edge; a bolted iron stair rises corner to corner through all three tiers, seen from a gallery at half height, looking down across the beds.

A glasshouse built inside a fort casemate, glass roofing the vaulted gun gallery in beaded wet panes that follow the barrel vault overhead and run off both top corners while the raw stone embrasures fill the flanks; a brass spiral stair climbs the inner pier to a slatted catwalk running the full length under the ridge, seen from the catwalk, looking down through the leaves.

A stepped glass ziggurat, each square storey set back from the one below, its riveted iron corners rising tier by tier and the uppermost glazed cap running off the top of the frame; the nearest pier fills the left edge, slim glazing ribs fanning outward across every face, beaded wet panes catching the light on each receding shelf; a bolted iron stair climbs the near face between the tiers, seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs.

A glasshouse built along the top of a railway viaduct, its glazed roof riding the arches, the curved iron ridge beam crossing the upper frame and the flanking panes running off both top corners while the viaduct's brick haunches anchor the ironwork below; slim riveted ribs repeat the arch of every span, beaded wet glass filling each bay; a cast-iron stair winds up the near pier through an arched opening, seen from the foot of the stair, looking up into the roof.

A circular glass rotunda crowned by a glazed cupola on a ring of iron columns, the cupola's ribbed dome filling the upper frame and running off both top corners, slim glazing ribs fanning down through wet panes to the ring-beam, each iron column a riveted shaft below; a running board at waist height circles the colonnade on brass brackets, its duckboard planking level with the column capitals, seen from the far end looking along the rotunda obliquely.

A glasshouse with a glazed observatory turret on its ridge reached by an iron stair, the turret's faceted panes rising into the upper-right corner of the frame, its riveted iron collar sitting on the ridge-beam while the main nave's arching ribs cross the top and run off the left edge; a plank gallery on brass brackets rings the turret base, seen from under the nearest arch looking up and across obliquely.

A glass cage built around one giant tree, the crown pressing on the panes overhead and the riveted iron uprights rising at each corner while the glazed roof runs off both top corners of the frame; slim glazing ribs angle between the uprights to follow the crown's spread, beaded wet panes filling every panel; a chain-hoist hangs from the ridge iron and a ring catwalk on brass brackets circles the trunk at canopy height, seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across.

A bell-shaped glass dome flaring out at its foot, the ribs curving like a bell mouth and sweeping wide before they tighten overhead, their riveted flanges catching the light; the wet panes fill the upper frame and run off both top corners while the flared skirt of glass closes the near edge, a railed inspection walk circling the waist on brass brackets, seen from the sunken bed, looking up and along the curving ribs.

A glasshouse stepped up in pagoda tiers with upturned glazed eaves, each tier's iron ring-beam carrying curved panes that kick out at their lower edge before the next storey rises; the nearest eave crosses the upper-right of the frame and the top tier runs off the corner, stone steps with a brass handrail climbing the near flank between the tiers, seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across the stacked rings.

A hot-wall house against a flue-warmed brick wall, its glazed slope leaning on the warm brick and the slim glazing ribs fanning up to a ridge iron, the beaded wet panes filling the upper frame and running off the top-right corner while the brick wall closes the whole left edge; a slatted catwalk runs the length under the ridge on riveted brackets, seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs.

A spherical glass bubble house floating on a pond, reached by a plank walk, its riveted iron meridians curving from the water-ring up and over and off the top of the frame, the beaded wet panes rounding across the upper two-thirds of the picture and the brass equatorial ring-beam crossing at mid-height; a brass spiral stair climbs the inner curve from the entry hatch, seen from the foot of the stair, looking up into the roof.

A vast flat glass roof carried on a forest of slender iron columns, the columns receding in rows into the far distance and the broad glazed plane crossing the top of the frame and running off both upper corners, slim glazing ribs dividing the panes in even lines above; a ladder-stair climbs the nearest column to a narrow catwalk under the roof glass, seen from the far end, looking along the house obliquely.

A nave whose end wall is a rose window of coloured glass throwing colour down the beds, amber and cobalt falling in lozenges across the brick path and vine rods below, the window's iron tracery filling the far end while the barrel-vaulted glazing ribs arch overhead and the wet side panes run off both edges; a running board at waist height lines the near flank, seen from a gallery at half height looking down across the beds.

A house with a glass floor over a brick cistern, black water and reflections shimmering below the iron grating the beds stand on, the cistern's brick walls just visible in the depths and the doubled image of every rib rising from the dark; the curved glazed roof fills the upper frame and runs off the top-right corner, the near glazed wall crossing the left edge, a brass spiral stair climbing the pier beside the arch, seen from under the nearest arch, obliquely.

A dome carried on one central iron tree whose cast branches spread outward to meet the encircling ribs, the trunk rising from brick floor to crown in a single shaft and the branch-joints riveted where each rib locks on; the dome's beaded wet panes fill the upper frame and run off the top corners, slim glazing ribs fanning between them, a cast-iron stair winding up around the trunk on scrolled brackets, seen from the sunken bed, looking up and along.

A glass rotunda around a tiered stone fountain playing at its centre, the curved ring of panes enclosing the full frame and the iron ring-beam crossing the top, slim riveted ribs rising from a low dwarf wall and fanning into the lantern above; the fountain's upper basin catches the light through the wet glass, a railed inspection walk running the full circumference on bolted iron brackets at canopy height, seen from the catwalk, looking down through the leaves.

A glass range running along three walls of a walled kitchen garden, its lean-to roofs meeting at two ridge valleys and the long glazed flank filling the right edge of the frame from corner to corner, riveted iron rafters fanning up to the wall-plate and slim glazing ribs between, brick piers anchoring each bay; a bolted iron stair rises at the near corner to the ridge walk, seen from beside the walkway looking diagonally across the range.

A long house with a wind-pump turning at its end, the sails seen through the gable glass filling the far frame; the curved glazed roof arcs up and off both top corners and the wet riveted flank runs the full length past the right edge, slim glazing ribs fanning between the panes overhead; stone steps with a brass handrail climb the near pier, seen from a gallery at half height, looking down across the beds.

A glasshouse of horseshoe Moorish arches in cast iron, the glass set in latticed panes whose beaded leads fill every bay; the arches stack and multiply upward, their riveted haunches running off both top corners of the frame and the nearest latticed pane crossing the whole right edge, a plank gallery on brass brackets ringing the drum above the springing line; seen from the foot of the stair, looking up into the roof.

A glass nave with a second nave crossing beneath it, seen down through a floor of glass set in riveted iron T-bars; the upper nave's slim glazing ribs fan overhead and arc off both top corners, the lower house pale and blue beyond the glass floor, a ladder-stair dropping through a hinged trap in the nearest pier; seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs.

A glasshouse roofing a stone crypt, the vault columns standing in the beds, their cut-stone caps rising through the brick floor into the iron superstructure above; the riveted ribs arc off both top corners and the beaded wet panes fill the upper frame, a slatted catwalk spanning column to column on brass brackets at capital height; seen from the sunken bed, looking up and along.

A glasshouse with a tall brick boiler chimney rising straight up through its roof, the stack's corbelled cap breaking the ridge and the surrounding panes cut and leaded tight around the brickwork; the glazed barrel arcs off both top corners and the riveted flank fills the right edge, a chain-hoist hanging beside the chimney and a ring catwalk circling it on iron arms; seen from under the nearest arch, obliquely.

Three domes in a row joined by short glazed links, each dome a different size, the nearest and largest filling the right half of the frame with its riveted iron ribs fanning to a crown that runs off the top edge, the middle dome's link glazing crossing low behind it, the smallest dome going pale in the distance; a brass spiral stair rises through the first link, seen from the far end, looking along the house obliquely.

A glazed pyramid on a square iron base, the ribs meeting at a single point high above, each triangular face a grid of slim glazing bars whose beaded panes run off all four top corners of the frame, the square iron base-ring crossing the lower middle distance on riveted brackets bolted to brick piers; a chain-hoist hangs the ring catwalk at mid-height on four iron rods, seen from the catwalk, looking down through the leaves.

A glasshouse whose floor is a spiral ramp rising round a central pier to the roof, its riveted iron pier climbing the full height of the frame while the curved glazed walls arc off both top corners in beaded wet panes, slim glazing ribs fanning outward at every turn of the ramp; a railed inspection walk rings the pier just below the ridge on brass brackets, seen from a gallery at half height, looking down across the beds.

A long house with a narrow tram track running down its floor and a flat truck on it, the barrel-vaulted glazed roof arcing up and off both top corners of the frame, riveted iron ribs spanning overhead and slim glazing ribs crossing the panes in a regular grid, the truck's brass fittings catching the light below; a running board at waist height runs the full flank of the truck, seen from the foot of the stair, looking up into the roof.

A glasshouse spanning a railway cutting, the glazed roof bridging from rim to rim above the rails, its riveted iron ribs arcing up and off both top corners of the frame while slim glazing ribs fan across the wet panes overhead and the brick cutting-walls drop away on each flank; a ladder-stair bolted to the near pier climbs to a narrow inspection walk under the ridge, seen from the sunken bed, looking up and along the ribs.

A horseshoe-plan house curving around an open pool, the glass on the inner face, its curved panes filling the right two-thirds of the frame and the iron ring-beam crossing the top while riveted arch-ribs step away into the curve; a plank gallery on brass brackets runs the full inner arc at mid-height, seen from under the nearest arch, obliquely, looking along the curving glass wall.

A great dome standing inside a ring of water, reached by an iron footbridge, its riveted ribs rising from broad brick piers and arcing off the upper frame while beaded wet panes fill the sky between them and the footbridge's grating crosses the near foreground; a bolted iron stair climbs the nearest pier to a slatted catwalk circling the drum, seen from the floor beside the nearest pier, looking up along the ribs.

A sunken glass corridor under a lawn, only its ridge showing above the grass, the slim glazing ribs fanning down each flank and the wet panes running off both top corners of the frame while the brick side-walls drop to a duckboard floor below; a slatted catwalk runs the full length just under the ridge on brass brackets, seen from the far end, looking along the house obliquely.

A glasshouse stepped down a hillside in four glazed terraces, each roof lower than the last, the nearest glazed pitch filling the upper-right of the frame and its riveted iron purlin crossing the top while the descending ridge-lines step away into the middle distance; stone steps with a brass handrail descend between each terrace, seen from beside the walkway, looking diagonally across the stepping roofs.
